summary: The model exhibits severe non-invariance to atom ordering at Layer 6 for physicochemical properties.

claims.claim: Layer 6 predictions are not permutation invariant for logP and TPSA.
claims.test: Apply RDKit canonicalization to a set of molecules; if the model is truly graph-invariant, drift should approach 0.
claims.prediction: Drift will remain high unless positional encodings are removed or graph topology is used directly without string ordering.

claims.claim: QED predictions are more robust to atom ordering than logP/TPSA.
claims.evidence: drift_over_mae for QED (2.20) is lower than logP (6.95) and TPSA (6.53).
claims.test: Compare drift on molecules with identical atom counts but different topologies.
claims.prediction: QED drift should be lower if the target aggregates multiple features that dilute sequence noise.

claims.claim: The model relies on SMILES token sequence rather than pure graph topology for Layer 6.
claims.evidence: High drift when only SMILES order changes (doRandom=True).
claims.test: Check if input is SMILES string or atom-indexed adjacency matrix.
claims.prediction: If input is SMILES string, drift is expected. If input is graph, drift implies positional encoding bias.

trivial_explanations: Atom counts are invariant to permutation; the high drift proves the model does not simply count atoms (which would yield 0 drift).
The properties logP and TPSA are additive/fragment-based in standard definitions (Crippen/Ertl); high drift suggests the model fails to learn these additive rules robustly.
